questiontext.text:
Goal

A ledger is one book of records divided into pages. Two agents hold different groups of pages, but both groups still belong to the same ledger.

Read
  • Arrays, slices (and strings). Under "Slices: The slice header", find the sliceHeader for slice2. Which array contains its ZerothElement? Does creating the slice copy any elements?
  • On the same page, find "Passing slices to functions". What does the caller see after AddOneToEachElement returns? What can the function not change in the SubtractOneFromLength example?
Coming from Java

A Java developer might make a defensive copy with new ArrayList<>(ledger.subList(from, to)). That gives the caller separate storage. The copy is banned here, and a hidden test writes through the page.

List<Integer> page = new ArrayList<>(ledger.subList(from, to));
Banned: copy
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • In the sliceHeader for slice2, find the target of ZerothElement. Is there a second array in that section?
  • Inspect AddOneToEachElement. What does the caller print after that function returns?

testcode.text: // rules
ledger := []int{10, 20, 30, 40, 50} p := page(ledger, 1, 3) redact(p) fmt.Println(ledger, p)
ledger := []int{10, 20, 30, 40, 50} p := page(ledger, 2, 5) redact(p[:1]) fmt.Println(ledger, p, len(p), len(ledger))
ledger := []int{10, 20, 30, 40} short := trim(ledger) redact(short) fmt.Println(len(ledger), len(short), ledger, short)

questiontext.text:
Goal

A duplex is one building divided into two homes. This landlord divides one hallway into flat A at the front and flat B at the back. Adding a room to flat A must not overwrite part of flat B.

Read
  • Slice expressions. Under "Full slice expressions", read the first paragraph and the a[1:3:5] example. What does the third index set? What length and capacity does t have?
  • Under "Simple slice expressions", find the sentence beginning "For slices, the upper index bound". Does len or cap bound a slice expression on a slice?
  • append. Read the first three sentences. When does append reuse the destination array? What does it do when it cannot reuse the array?
Coming from Java

In Java, new ArrayList<>(hall.subList(0, k)) creates a fresh list with separate storage. This task bans that copy. Both flats must remain parts of one hallway.

List<String> flatA = new ArrayList<>(hall.subList(0, k));
Banned: copy, make, append
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Under "Full slice expressions", find how the third index sets capacity.
  • Find the spare capacity of a plain hall[:k]. What does append do when that capacity is available?

testcode.text: // rules
a, b := partition([]string{"foyer", "study", "kitchen", "bath"}) fmt.Println(a, b)
hall := []string{"foyer", "study", "kitchen"} a, b := partition(hall) a[0] = "lounge" fmt.Println(a, b, hall)
hall := []string{"foyer", "study", "kitchen", "bath"} a, b := partition(hall) a = append(a, "shed") fmt.Println(a, b, hall)

expected.text: [foyer study shed] [kitchen bath] [foyer study kitchen bath]

testcode.text: hall := []string{"foyer", "study", "kitchen", "bath", "attic"} a, b := partition(hall) fmt.Println(len(a), cap(a), len(b), cap(b)) b = append(b, "shed") a = append(a, "porch") fmt.Println(a, b, hall)

expected.text: 2 2 3 3 [foyer study porch] [kitchen bath attic shed] [foyer study kitchen bath attic]

questiontext.text:
Goal

A signals desk writes incoming messages on a fixed-size pad and keeps the newest message at the top of its board. A snapshot is a saved view of the board. It must not change when later messages arrive.

Read
  • copy. Read the last sentence. If the destination is shorter than the source, how many elements are copied? What does the return value count?
  • Read the preceding sentence in the same documentation. Can the source and destination share storage?
  • Arrays, slices (and strings), section "Copy". In the Insert example, which direction does copy move the upper part of the slice? What does the preceding paragraph say about overlap?
Coming from Java

Java's System.arraycopy throws when the destination is too short. Arrays.copyOf allocates a destination. Go's copy handles both jobs.

System.arraycopy(msgs, 0, pad, 0, msgs.length);
Banned: for. Required: copy
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • For snapshot, compare the last documentation sentence with the length of a destination declared only with var.
  • For pin, find the copy call in the Insert example. Compare its two arguments with yours.

testcode.text: // rules
board := []string{"alpha", "bravo"} saved := snapshot(board) board[0] = "zulu" fmt.Println(saved, board)
pad := []string{"-", "-"} n := record(pad, []string{"alpha", "bravo", "charlie"}) fmt.Println(n, pad) fmt.Println(record(pad, nil), pad)
board := []string{"alpha", "bravo", "charlie", "delta"} saved := snapshot(board) pin(board, "echo") pin(board, "foxtrot") fmt.Println(board, saved, len(snapshot(nil)))

expected.text: [foxtrot echo alpha bravo] [alpha bravo charlie delta] 0

questiontext.text:
Goal

A market stall displays its prices on a board. An AI rewrote the board's program with three loops that count from zero by hand. The tests pass, but the stallholder wants range loops before using it.

Read
  • For statements with range clause. Read the table row for a slice. What two iteration values does it produce?
  • Read the first paragraph of the same section. How does an iteration value reach its variable? Does changing that variable change the slice?
  • Find the paragraph after the table and the sentence beginning "For an array, pointer to array, or slice value a". At which index do iteration values start? Which value does a loop with one variable receive?
Coming from Java

A Java developer might use the counted loop below and reserve the enhanced for loop for code that does not need an index. The starter code repeats the counted loop three times.

for (int i = 0; i < prices.size(); i++) {
    prices.set(i, prices.get(i) * (100 - pct) / 100);
}
Required: range
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Check the second range value for a slice. For each function, decide whether the loop needs the index, the element, or both.
  • For discount, how must the assignment use the slice if the iteration variable receives a copy?

testcode.text: // rules
board := []int{25, 40, 60} fmt.Println(total(board), cheapest(board))
fmt.Println(cheapest([]int{}), cheapest([]int{3, 9, 3}), total(nil))
board := []int{7, 7, 2} fmt.Println(cheapest(board)) discount(board, 50) fmt.Println(board, cheapest(board)) discount(board, 100) fmt.Println(board, cheapest(board))
